messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Correctable ECC error rate rising across inference pool in us-west-2. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered. ticket=INC-2026-3345 :rotating_light:

maria: ack - I'm on it. seeing initial spike from telemetry around 3351234500. Noted higher driver resets/Xid on some nodes.

jamal: which nodes? any customer impact yet?

maria: nodes: gpu-usw2-az1-12, gpu-usw2-az1-14, gpu-usw2-az3-03. telemetry shows Xid 79 / nv-host-reset in dmesg and short container crashes (OOM not primary). latency alerts for a few hosted routes (chat/generate) spiking 3-5x.

sophia: grabbing logs from the first node. running: 
```sh
dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i xid
# and
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
```

raj: paging PGs show a pattern of correctable -> driver reset -> short flapping. Not seeing permanent hardware panics (no machine reboot).

maria: mitigation plan: 1) cordonsuspect nodes 2) drain pods serving inference 3) route traffic to fallback pool (cpu/other-gpu-pool) 4) collect nvml, dmesg, kernel logs for offline triage.

jamal: +1. I'll take cordon/drain for az1-12/14. maria, you grab az3-03.

maria: executing now: 
```sh
kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-az1-12
kubectl drain gpu-usw2-az1-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

deploy-bot: rollouts:route-change detected -> shifting 25% traffic off gpu-usw2 to fallback-pool (cpu-fallback). runbook:failover-step-3 applied.

sophia: dmesg snippets from az1-12: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=1345, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679001] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU reset: RSR:0x9 
```

raj: nvidia-smi shows ECC correctable counters increasing rapidly on GPU 0 and 1. nv_host_reset counts incrementing.

jamal: observed some pods going CrashLoopBackOff with OOMKilled after reset. Looks like driver reset caused process memory accounting issues. Need to evict gracefully.

maria: customer impact - Hosting: small % of requests returned 5xx/timeout for a few customers on shared plan; Dedicated customers with pinned nodes unaffected so far. Notifying CS to inform impacted customers.

sophia: collecting full diagnostic bundle. running: 
```sh
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-usw2-az1-12
journalctl -k -n 500 | grep -i nvrm > /tmp/az1-12-nvrm.log
/etc/collect_gpu_diag.sh gpu-usw2-az1-12 > /tmp/diag-az1-12.tar.gz
```

jamal: drain complete for az1-12 and az1-14. pods rescheduled to fallback pool. latency baseline returning closer to normal.

maria: cordon+drain for az3-03 done. traffic >90% routed off affected nodes. continuing telemetry watch.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: Severity=SEV2 -> mitigated (partial). Auto-suppressing noisy alerts for these nodes for 15m.

raj: quick checks: kernel module version matches expected prod driver 530.41.03. No recent driver upgrades in last deploy window.

jamal: marked nodes for tighter monitoring and scheduled soft-reboot out-of-band overnight if counters don't decrease. Opening hardware ticket with provider for ECC trending.

maria: next actions: 1) preserve diag bundle and upload to /mnt/incident/3351234567/ 2) coordinate brief for CS + oncall handoff in 15m 3) if counters keep rising -> consider cordoning whole AZ and draining to spare region.

sophia: diag upload done: s3://redwood-incidents/3351234567/diag-az1-12.tar.gz (logs, nvidia-smi -q, dmesg, kubectl describe outputs)

raj: note for postmortem - track correlation of batch workloads + sustained long sequence lengths -> prefix cache pressure maybe exposing kernel driver bug. Add quantization/sequence length tags to telemetry.

jamal: i'm taking the on-call handoff in 15m. maria, can you add a short summary for the bridge and CS?

maria: summary for bridge: "Correctable ECC errors causing intermittent driver resets (Xid 79) on 3 nodes in us-west-2. Nodes cordoned and drained, traffic routed to fallback pool. Diagnostics collected; CS notified for limited customer impact (increased 5xx/timeouts for shared hosts). Monitoring continues; handoff to jamal in 15m."

sophia: quick snippet for CS: "We observed elevated GPU ECC corrected errors that led to driver resets on a subset of GPU nodes resulting in short-lived request errors. We've drained affected nodes and routed traffic to fallback capacity. Engineers have collected diagnostics and are monitoring. No data loss reported."

jamal: taking handoff. action items for next shift: keep nodes cordoned, wait for ECC counters to stabilize for 6 hours, if trend persists -> escalate to hardware and consider replacement. create follow-up incident ticket for PM/infra review.

maria: thanks everyone. leaving oncall notes in the ticket and marking as mitigated for now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: INC-2026-3345; severity downgraded -> MONITOR. Please update ticket with remediation and postmortem link when available. :white_check_mark:

maria: closing thread on Slack, will update if status changes. jamal, ping me if you need anything during handoff.
